summary: The forward merge only: GitHub reported #2504 CONFLICTING with main again, which would have refused READY, so main at 96a7e5ea is merged in with two conflicts resolved (internal/bus/recovery.go's onReconnect and packages/envoy/infra/README.md's alarm paragraph, each keeping both sides). No behaviour of this pull request changed; the acceptance evidence at 999ce53f stands.

proof.criterion: The merge keeps both sides' behaviour where they meet in code: this branch's markHooksDueLocked still counts the connection event the reconnect hooks must cover, and main's clearPublishDenials still runs on the same reconnect.
proof.surface: The repository's Go test harness for the packages the conflict touches, over a real embedded NATS: internal/bus (the reconnect, recovery and hook-stall tests), internal/kvwatch and cmd/listener.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go build ./... && go vet ./internal/bus/ ./internal/kvwatch/ ./cmd/listener/ && go test -p 2 -parallel 4 ./internal/bus/ ./internal/kvwatch/ -count=1 -timeout 30m && go test -p 2 -parallel 4 ./cmd/listener/ -count=1 -timeout 40m -skip '<the four Docker-only TestDispatch tests>'
proof.observed: build and vet exit 0; ok internal/bus 309.937s, ok internal/kvwatch 62.509s, ok cmd/listener 435.807s. internal/bus's suite is the one that covers both halves of the resolved line: the hook-stall tests read what markHooksDueLocked recorded, and main's publish-denial tests exercise clearPublishDenials on the same reconnect.
proof.negativeControl: The unresolved merge is the control: with jj's conflict markers in place the tree does not compile (go build fails in internal/bus/recovery.go), so the build above passes only because both statements were kept; dropping either side's line is a compile error or a silently lost call that the bus suite's hook-stall and publish-denial tests catch.

proof.criterion: The merged alarm paragraph still renders as the AWS reference expects, so this change's reconnect-hooks-stalled alarm and main's new publish-failure wording coexist.
proof.surface: The separate packages/envoy/infra Go module, whose tests render a WebhookListener's children and compare them with the reference list.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -p 2 -parallel 4 ./aws/... ./render/... -count=1
proof.observed: build and vet exit 0; ok infra/aws 4.852s, ok infra/aws/rendering 0.010s, ok infra/render 0.138s.
proof.negativeControl: The reference list in infra/aws/webhooklistener_test.go is the control: it is one of the eight files main also changed in this window, and a resolution that dropped this change's signal from the production list, or main's from the reference, fails that comparison.

proof.criterion: The round is classified as the architect's rule asks, so the right checks are read at this head.
proof.surface: The branch's own diff against its base, and the file-name intersection of main's merged window with this pull request's files.
proof.command: jj diff --from "fork_point(main@origin | <head>)" --to <head> --git --context 0 '~(.legion | docs/solutions)' | sed -e '/^@@/d' -e '/^index /d' | sha256sum, at f140c718 and again at 4f22b8aa; and comm -12 of jj diff --from 3c2691a7 --to 96a7e5ea --name-only with the pull request's own file list
proof.observed: Fingerprint f85181b8... to 8070cbb3..., changed. Main's window is 341 files, the pull request 24, and the intersection is eight: docs/site/src/content/docs/dispatch/envoy.md, packages/envoy/AGENTS.md, packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md, packages/envoy/infra/README.md, packages/envoy/infra/aws/rendering/metricfilters.go, packages/envoy/infra/aws/webhooklistener_test.go, packages/envoy/internal/bus/nats.go, packages/envoy/internal/bus/recovery.go. Both tests say a full round, so the listener lanes are the ones to read at this head and the suites above were all re-run.
proof.negativeControl: The merge at 0ae1b454 is the contrast: its fingerprint did not move, yet main had changed three of this pull request's files, which is the case that made the architect add the intersection test; here both tests agree.

filesChanged: packages/envoy/internal/bus/recovery.go: the conflict in onReconnect resolved - this branch's c.markHooksDueLocked() where c.connEvents++ was, then main's comment and c.clearPublishDenials() unchanged.

packages/envoy/infra/README.md: the conflict in the listener's alarm paragraph resolved - this branch's <N>-reconnect-hooks-stalled entry kept in the list, main's new sentences about <N>-publish-failure and <N>-webhook-refused kept after it, main's closing sentence kept.
Nothing else: this round is the forward merge only.
trickyParts: The two sides met inside one statement list in onReconnect, so the resolution had to keep this branch's replacement of c.connEvents++ and main's two added lines in main's order; a resolution that took either side whole loses a call.
discoveredComplexity: main changed eight of this pull request's 24 files in one window, five of them documentation; the pull request's own fingerprint moved only because two of them conflicted. That is why the round is full rather than a confirmation.
